easy: Easier than an even game; the best level for learning
standard: About an even game with two to four rivals; a little tougher with five
hard: About as strong as the app's rivals
method: Each cell is 360 games on seeds (block 200000) not used to tune the rules, played with v0.4.0 (rival tie-break). Lower means tougher rivals. In a perfectly even game the player would win 33% against two rivals, 25% against three, 20% against four and 17% against five.
strategy: **Strategy balance.** Chasing Domination cards is still the strongest simple approach: at Standard it wins 15–44% against 2–25% for spreading out or chasing majorities. A self-tuned test player that fights for turn order and Domination spaces does better still, about 20 points above the card-chaser at Standard, which is the same margin it gets against the app's rivals. Before the rival tie-break that margin was about 40 points.
stalls: No test game stalled: every game reached a normal end. If the action display fills before every rival has placed, Planning simply ends and the extra pawns wait for the next turn.
